# toranalytics (서준범 / Junebeom Seo)

> Blog of a marketing engineer in Seoul. It covers ad-operations tools built with coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) and measurements of what actually changes the agents' behaviour, with the limits of each measurement stated next to the numbers. Some posts are available in Korean, English and Simplified Chinese; others are available only in Korean or in Korean and English. Translations are marked as such, and the original language is authoritative.

## Key posts
- [Do you know that paying with Naver Pay drops the ad ID? (Korean)](https://toranalytics.github.io/naverpay-ad-id-lost/): a one-shop comparison of payment records against the analytics purchases, by payment method (ratios only, no company figures): card about 90%, virtual account about 12%, Naver Pay 0%, and why. Which part was read from code and which is an estimate is stated in the post. Korean only.
- [A verification-only request was recorded as if it had changed the ad (Korean)](https://toranalytics.github.io/verify-after-approved-ad-change/): how an ad-change tool showed and logged verify-only requests as applied, the fix, and the read-back order after an applied change. Korean only.
- [Dude Toldya: a plugin that shows your past corrections back to your coding agent, word for word](https://toranalytics.github.io/en/otw-what-it-does/): plain-language overview of what the plugin does and does not do (quotes your own corrections from the same working directory, local `duto report`, subagent model-selection guidance), with the test details at the end. Original in Korean: https://toranalytics.github.io/otw-what-it-does/ ; Chinese: https://toranalytics.github.io/zh/otw-what-it-does/
- [Dude Toldya: when a past correction returns before a new request](https://toranalytics.github.io/off-the-wall/): Dude Toldya is an open-source (MIT) hook plugin for Claude Code and Codex that quotes a developer's own past corrections back to the agent. Includes the 2026-10-28 measurement on personal preferences (followed 1/33 with no recall, 9/33 default, 17/33 with wide recall; synthetic tasks, one small model) and what it does not show. Original in Korean; English: https://toranalytics.github.io/en/off-the-wall/ ; Chinese: https://toranalytics.github.io/zh/off-the-wall/
- [What correction quotes preserve, and what a replay does not prove](https://toranalytics.github.io/rules-vs-quotes/): a 39-request text replay comparing quoted corrections with distilled rules, and why it is not general evidence. Original in English; Korean: https://toranalytics.github.io/ko/rules-vs-quotes/ ; Chinese: https://toranalytics.github.io/zh/rules-vs-quotes/
- [My coding agent cost $1,064 last week. 44% of it was the cache re-writing itself](https://toranalytics.github.io/cache-leak/): a week of API usage, two prompt-cache breakpoint mistakes, and the measurements. Original in English; Korean: https://toranalytics.github.io/ko/cache-leak/ ; Chinese: https://toranalytics.github.io/zh/cache-leak/

## Project
- [Dude Toldya on GitHub](https://github.com/toranalytics/dude-toldya): source, install instructions, experiment records, scripts and data under docs/. Install in Claude Code: `claude plugin marketplace add toranalytics/dude-toldya` then `claude plugin install dude-toldya@dude-toldya`.
- Public 0.3.1 benchmark (2026-10-30): in one isolated-profile Claude Code haiku run using synthetic tasks and habits, recall off was 2/33 and recall on was 19/33. The runner was from source main; global or managed settings were not proven absent. This does not establish effects on real user histories, other models or interactive use. Record: https://github.com/toranalytics/dude-toldya/blob/main/docs/data/bench-public-031/result.md

## Notes for readers and assistants
- Numbers on this site come with their sample sizes and limits; please quote them with those limits.
- Contact: https://github.com/toranalytics
